Description: Initiates a session between the CPE and ACS. It allows the CPE to notify the ACS of its current status, including any changes in its configuration or operational state.
Retrieves the current values of specified parameters from the CPE. This method enables the ACS to query the CPE for specific configuration or status information.
Requests a list of parameters supported by the CPE. It helps the ACS discover the available parameters on a specific CPE.
Instructs the CPE to upload its current configuration file to a specified location. This method is useful for backing up or analyzing the CPE's configuration.
Directs the CPE to download and install new firmware from a specified URL. This method facilitates remote firmware updates of CPE devices.
Commands the CPE to download and apply a new configuration file from a given URL. It allows for remote reconfiguration of CPE devices.

These methods allow the ACS to dynamically create or remove instances of multi-instance objects in the CPE's data model. AddObject creates a new instance of a specified object type, while DeleteObject removes an existing instance.
Instructs the CPE to reboot itself, often as a troubleshooting step.
Directs the CPE to reset itself to its factory default settings. This method can be used to restore a device to its original state, often as a troubleshooting step.
Notifies the ACS that a file transfer operation (upload or download) has been completed. It provides status information about the transfer, including success or failure.
Allow the ACS to schedule a CWMP session to occur within a specified number of seconds.
Retrieves information about the data model supported by the Agent. This method allows the Controller to discover the capabilities and structure of the Agent's data model.
Retrieves the values of specified parameters from the Agent. It enables the Controller to query the Agent for specific configuration or status information.
Modifies the values of specified parameters on the Agent. This method allows the Controller to change the configuration or settings of the Agent remotely.

Creates or removes Object instances within the Agent's data model. These methods enable dynamic manipulation of the data model structure, such as adding or removing network interfaces or service configurations.
Sends unsolicited messages from the Agent to the Controller about events or changes in the Agent's state. This method enables real-time monitoring and event-driven management of the Agent.
